title: Introduction to the Club & CTF Basics
description: Overview of the club and basic team roles, followed by a simple introductory CTF game covering foundational computer science and light security concepts.

title: Introduction to Cyber Competitions
description: A look at how a typical team defense competition works using examples from past events. Covers team structure and basic roles.

title: Virtualization & Introduction to the Command Line
description: Why we use the command line, basic Linux navigation, and text editing. Setting up local VMs and using online practice labs like OverTheWire.

title: Understanding File Systems
description: Command line practice using the club's practice range. Finding configuration files and system logs, and comparing how Linux and Windows organize files.

title: Remote Access Basics: SSH & RDP
description: How developers and admins log into servers remotely, covering SSH keys and remote desktop connections, and their vulnerabilities.

title: Basic Networking & Communication
description: Introduction to IP addresses, subnets, and local networks. Mapping basic network blocks using tools like nmap, Packet Tracer, and Wireshark.

title: Operating System Permissions & Access Control
description: Understanding user accounts, groups, administration rights (sudo), and file permissions on both Linux and Windows.

title: Basic Host Hardening
description: Reviewing user account lists, removing unnecessary accounts, and locking down permissions on practice hosts.

title: System Services & Background Processes
description: A look at Windows services, the registry, Linux system processes, and scheduled tasks.

title: Finding Unwanted Processes
description: Searching for simple backdoors, checking active system tasks, disabling unneeded services, and cleaning up unauthorized scheduled actions on the range.

title: Network Monitoring & Traffic Basics
description: Looking at network packet structures, protocol headers, and using basic monitoring tools like tcpdump.

title: Analyzing Traffic for Incidents
description: Using Wireshark on the range to review recorded network traffic and find unencrypted credentials or standard scanning signatures.

title: Web Infrastructure Basics: DNS
description: How domain name resolution works, managing zones and basic records, and setting up a simple DNS server inside a local VM.

title: DNS Auditing & Configuration Check
description: Checking basic domain controller configurations and fixing common misconfigurations on the practice range.

title: Mid-Semester Practice Simulation
description: A short practice run: 30 minutes to set up, 30 minutes defending a basic environment with help from club alumni, and 30 minutes to review.

title: Introduction to Active Directory
description: Why organizations centralize user management, covering Windows Server domains, organizational units, and basic trust setups.

title: Active Directory Basics & Policy Controls
description: Reviewing administrative rights on the range and using Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to apply standard security settings.

title: Web & Database Server Setup
description: Standard system administration steps: installing Apache or Nginx web servers, connecting them to a SQL database backend, and basic user permissions.

title: Application Security & Log Review
description: Securing the web and database setup on the range, adjusting access controls, and checking web server logs for irregular entries.

title: Introduction to Log Collection
description: Understanding system logs, Windows Event IDs, and how systems send logs across a network for centralized storage.

title: Basic Centralized Monitoring
description: Setting up simple monitoring agents (like Security Onion or Wazuh) on the range to collect data and view basic dashboards.

title: Basic Automation: Scripting
description: Writing straightforward diagnostic scripts using a combination of Go, Python, Bash, and PowerShell to check system status.

title: Using Scripts for Configuration Checks
description: Running simple verification scripts across a few range hosts to check for unauthorized files or system changes.

title: System Backups & Recovery Planning
description: Looking at backup strategies, system snapshots, and general recovery steps for keeping services running.

title: System Recovery Practice
description: An incident response exercise on the range focused on recovering standard web services or configurations from clear backups.

title: Competition Workflow & Communication
description: How teams organize tasks under tight timelines: prioritizing incoming requests, tracking configuration changes, and maintaining simple logs.

title: Open Lab Project Day & Catch-up
description: An open session managed by officers for finishing hardware setups, troubleshooting scripts, practicing on the range, or reviewing basic strategy.

title: End-of-Term Practice Run
description: A final two-hour team defense exercise on the range featuring basic scenario updates, support from alumni, and a walk-through of the results.
